title: Memory of hypoxic events in solid tumors
question: I want to design a bacterial microrobot that resides in a solid tumor region, activates under hypoxia, and retains a record that it reached the tumor for a time after leaving the hypoxic area. Propose a complete biological circuit covering sensing, memory, output, and safety control. Assess its feasibility and principal risks.

title: Recording multiple signals in the tumor microenvironment
question: Design a biological microrobot that monitors a tumor microenvironment solely by recording whether it has encountered acidity, hypoxia, and inflammatory signals, without directly killing tumor cells. Decide whether it needs multi-input logic gates and memory, and choose a low-risk output.

title: Separating external-field navigation from local activation
question: I want a therapeutic tumor robot that navigates first and activates later. It should stay silent while an external field guides it and allow functional protein expression only after reaching the tumor region. Outline a high-level biological circuit and explain the respective roles of external control signals and endogenous tumor signals.

title: Distinguishing inflammation from tumor tissue using multiple signals
question: Design a biological microrobot that distinguishes ordinary inflamed tissue from tumor tissue by combining several environmental inputs. Provide a sensing, logic, and output architecture and explain which input signals are prone to misclassification.

title: Long-term recording of tumor recurrence signals
question: I want a microbial robot to monitor tumor recurrence. It has no therapeutic role. After sensing recurrence-associated signals in vivo, it should form a long-term record that can be read out. Design appropriate sensing, memory, and reporting modules and assess how long-term memory affects host burden and safety.

title: Low-risk reporting on the immune microenvironment
question: Design a biological microrobot that assesses whether the local immune environment in a tumor is immunosuppressive and produces a low-risk reporter signal. What categories of input signals should it use? Does it need logic gates or memory? Explain how to avoid overinterpreting therapeutic effects.

title: Output triggered by three concurrent conditions
question: I want a tumor robot whose output activates only when hypoxia, high lactate, and an external trigger occur together. Provide a module-level design and assess the benefits and costs of using three conditions instead of two.

title: Indirect sensing of the tumor stroma
question: Design a biological microrobot to sense tissue stiffening or abnormal extracellular matrix in the tumor stroma. The current database may have no direct mechanosensing component. Propose an alternative sensing strategy and explain how to label gaps in the evidence.

title: Short-term reporting of intestinal inflammation
question: I want a gut bacterial robot to monitor inflammatory bowel disease by sensing inflammation-associated signals and producing a detectable reporter signal within a short time. Design the circuit architecture and decide whether it needs long-term memory.

title: Temporal filtering for sustained inflammation
question: Design a gut-resident living therapeutic robot that distinguishes temporary dietary disturbances from sustained inflammation and activates its output only for a persistent abnormality. Design appropriate sensing, temporal filtering, memory, or logic modules and discuss relevant caveats.

title: Population-density feedback on expression in the gut
question: I want engineered bacteria in the gut to adjust expression to population density, avoiding ineffective expression at low density and excessive burden at high density. Design an architecture combining quorum-sensing communication and feedback control. Assess potential effects of population heterogeneity.

title: Detecting dysbiosis through metabolites
question: Design a microbial robot that detects gut dysbiosis by sensing metabolite changes and issuing a low-risk report without therapeutic intervention. Describe the sensing and output modules, evidence requirements, and risks of misclassification.

title: Single-event recording of abnormal gut exposure
question: I want a gut robot that retains a record after a single abnormal exposure, such as an inflammatory flare or a peak in a particular metabolite. Design a single-event memory circuit and readout, and assess whether irreversible memory is appropriate.

title: Conditional decisions amid complex gut signals
question: Design a living diagnostic robot for the gut that responds only to the target inflammatory state amid complex background signals. Decide whether it needs an AND gate, a NOT gate, or threshold-like control. Explain why a simple sensor linked to an output may be insufficient.

title: Long-term gut monitoring and low-burden control
question: I want an engineered bacterial robot that persists in the gut over the long term with minimal disruption to the microbiota. Design its safety controls, low-burden expression strategy, environmental sensing, and periodic status reporting. Identify which elements can currently be assessed only in a high-level design review.

title: Reviewing an early-warning design for children's gut health
question: Design a biological robot for early warning of intestinal inflammation in children. Given this more sensitive use case, specify stricter safety boundaries, output strategies, and evaluation criteria than for a typical adult application.

title: Monitoring chronic wound infection
question: I want a biological microrobot that recognizes bacterial infection signals in chronic wounds and produces a low-risk visual report. Design its sensing, decision logic, and reporter modules and explain how to avoid mistaking ordinary inflammation for infection.

title: Recording biofilm risk events
question: Design a microbial robot that recognizes early signals of biofilm formation. It should detect signals associated with collective behavior and record a single biofilm risk event. Propose quorum-sensing, memory, and output modules.

title: Grading wound risk using multiple inputs
question: I want a biological robot that assesses a wound by sensing pH, oxidative stress, and infection signals together and assigning a risk level. Design a multi-input circuit with graded decision logic rather than a single switch.

title: Early warning of implant surface infection
question: Design a biological microrobot for early warning of infection on an implant surface. It provides no treatment and issues a report only when it detects infection risk. Explain how you would design surface-associated sensing, memory, and safety restrictions.

title: Distinguishing acute infection from chronic inflammation over time
question: I want a biological robot that distinguishes acute infection from chronic low-level inflammation. Design temporal control logic, considering transient responses, sustained responses, or state retention, and explain how you would evaluate the rationale for the design.

title: Monitoring dental plaque
question: Design a microbial robot that monitors dental plaque by detecting local acidification and changes in microbial population density and producing a nontherapeutic readout. Describe the module architecture and relevant caveats.

title: Recording local oxidative stress events
question: I want engineered bacteria to serve as event recorders in a localized infection, logging whether they encountered high oxidative stress. Design a sensor–memory–reporter system and identify signals that could cause false positives.

title: Short-term monitoring of the skin microbiota
question: Design a biological robot for short-term monitoring of the skin microbiota. Its operation must be low-risk and reversible, and it should avoid long-term residence. Decide whether it needs memory and whether it needs a kill switch or self-limiting control.

title: Recognizing the thrombus microenvironment
question: I want a biological microrobot that recognizes the environment near a thrombus and distinguishes normal blood flow from a local coagulation or inflammatory microenvironment. Design its sensing, logic, reporter, and safety modules.

title: Capturing transient signals in fast flow
question: Design a biological microrobot for fast-flowing conditions where contact with the target area may be brief. Decide whether it needs a fast-response sensor, a short-term memory module, or an external trigger, and explain the design risks.

title: Low-burden reporting for vascular diagnosis
question: I want a diagnostic microrobot that travels through blood vessels. It cannot continuously express a burdensome output and should report only briefly upon detecting an abnormal signal. Design a control architecture with low background expression and low burden.

title: Recording local ischemic events
question: Design a biological microrobot that detects local ischemia by sensing oxygen changes and recording whether a hypoxic event occurred. Provide a high-level circuit design and evaluation metrics.

title: Separating magnetic actuation from local expression
question: I want an externally driven, magnetically responsive biological robot that keeps its functional modules silent in transit and expresses them only when local signals trigger it at the target. Design the layered logic linking external control to the biological circuit.

title: Recognizing inflamed plaques using multiple conditions
question: Design a biological robot that recognizes inflamed vascular plaques while avoiding an excessive response to systemic inflammatory signals. Design multi-input decision logic and a conservative output strategy.

title: Recording heavy metal exposure in a closed device
question: I want a biological microrobot that detects heavy metal pollution in water inside a closed test device and records whether it experienced high exposure. Design a sensor–memory–reporter architecture and explain why the system should be confined to the device.

title: Distinguishing pesticide residues in soil
question: Design a microbial robot for detecting pesticide residues in agricultural soil. It must distinguish the target contaminant from ordinary nutrient changes. Describe the sensing modules, decision logic, and output strategy.

title: Feedback control of reporting on wastewater pollution loads
question: I want a biological robot for a wastewater treatment plant that monitors the organic pollution load and adjusts reporter intensity through feedback. Design a sensing, feedback, and output architecture and discuss resource burden.

title: Classifying multiple contaminants and encoding outputs
question: Design a population of microbial robots that detects multiple contaminants and uses different reporters to convey different risk levels. Design multi-input classification logic and explain how to prevent interference among reporters.

title: Long-term recording of pollution exposure
question: I want an environmental microbial robot that leaves a long-term record after detecting a contaminant so the event can be read out later. Assess whether irreversible memory is appropriate and discuss containment risks.

title: Indirect sensing of microplastic-associated pollution
question: Design a biological robot to monitor pollution associated with marine microplastics. The database may have no direct microplastic sensor. Explain how to use indirect environmental signals in the design and indicate where evidence is insufficient.

title: Output design for detection-only tasks
question: I want an environmental robot that detects contaminants without degrading them. Design the output system and explain why you would omit degradation or remediation modules.

title: Short-term detection in a field sampling box
question: Design a microbial detection system for a field sampling box. It must be inexpensive, low-risk, and easy to read, with no need for long-term survival. Which modules can be simplified, and which safety modules must be retained?

title: Reporting metabolic state during fermentation
question: I want a cell-based robot that senses metabolite accumulation during fermentation and automatically reports production status. Design the sensing, output, and feedback modules and explain why memory may be unnecessary.

title: Stress feedback in industrial strains
question: Design a biological robot that monitors stress in an industrial strain, senses resource burden or stress, and reduces output when the burden becomes too high. Provide a feedback control architecture.

title: Distinguishing metabolic changes from stress in Yarrowia lipolytica
question: I want a monitoring system for metabolic engineering in Yarrowia lipolytica that distinguishes product accumulation from cellular stress. Design the sensing and reporting modules and explain why evidence from a different species cannot be directly extrapolated.

title: Switching states across biomanufacturing stages
question: Design an engineered bacterial robot for biomanufacturing process optimization that switches expression states across production stages. Describe stage control, sensing, and output, and explain the challenges of timing control.

title: Recording high-substrate shocks
question: I want a production-strain robot that records whether it experienced a sudden high substrate concentration. Design the memory module and readout and assess whether maintaining the record could affect production performance.

title: Reporting population state in fermentation
question: Design a population of microbial robots that monitors the collective state in a fermenter. It should use communication to report the population's overall state while filtering single-cell noise. Propose quorum sensing or another form of population-level control.

title: Feedback on product accumulation and expression burden
question: I want a production cell system that automatically reduces expression burden once the product reaches a certain level. Design a metabolic feedback control architecture and discuss the risk of oscillation or instability.

title: Stress-responsive regulation during protein production
question: Design a biological robot for protein production that automatically adjusts expression levels in response to cellular stress. Design a sensing, control, and output system and give evaluation metrics.

title: Monitoring the tissue scaffold microenvironment
question: I want a biological microrobot in a tissue engineering scaffold to sense local oxygen and nutrient conditions and report the microenvironment inside the scaffold. Design a sensor–output architecture and explain whether memory is needed.

title: Spatial expression patterns in biomaterials
question: Design an engineered cell system that forms spatial patterns inside a biomaterial by using local signals to decide whether to express proteins associated with structure. Propose a sensing, logic, and expression design and discuss spatial cross-talk.

title: Recording damage events in soft materials
question: I want a biological robot to monitor damage in a soft material by sensing changes in its surroundings and recording damage events. Design the sensing, memory, and readout modules and identify which signals are only indirect indicators.

title: Minimally disruptive monitoring of the organoid microenvironment
question: Design a biological robot for monitoring the microenvironment inside an organoid. It must be minimally disruptive, impose a low output burden, and distinguish hypoxia from nutrient deficiency. Provide a complete high-level design, evaluation metrics, and caveats.
